**Finding submitted: deviation (critical) — LOL-CAP.**

**What I found.** The Agreement has no limitation-of-liability section. The only cap language sits at the tail of the Section 12 indemnity (p0077) and is one-way:

- It caps **TrueLink only**, and only for matters under Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 — Client has **no cap at all**, despite the very broad indemnity it gives at Sections 12(a)(i)–(iv) (breach, customer acts, Web Site/Client Content, product/service injury).
- No exclusion of indirect/consequential damages anywhere (zero hits for "consequential").
- No carve-outs for confidentiality (Section 10) or either party's indemnification obligations; the basis is "compensation **paid**", not "paid or payable", with no floor.

Uncapped Customer liability against a capped Vendor is expressly walk-away territory under the rule, and the clause also fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with indemnity/confidentiality/gross negligence/wilful misconduct carve-outs).

**Redline (validated ok:true).** A single edit to p0077 rather than a new section: mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' hosting/support compensation paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; mutual indirect-damages exclusion; "Excluded Claims" carve-out for confidentiality/data security, indemnification under Section 12, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement; and Client's payment obligations excluded from "damages".

One trade worth flagging to the business: the mutual cap displaces the current section-limited TrueLink cap, so TrueLink gains a cap where it previously had none outside Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11. That exposure is largely preserved for us because TrueLink's Section 12(b) indemnity (which covers *any* breach by TrueLink of the Agreement) is an Excluded Claim and therefore sits outside the cap.
